newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat up on expiry related short-covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat up on expiry related short-covering.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil prices were moderately higher in Monday morning trade as the near expiry of the May contract triggered short-covering.
The short-covering, players said, gave a slight boost to flagging gasoline futures, which remain in negative territory due to ample supply.
"This morning's heating oil gains are mostly technical moves of the expiry on Wednesday," said one floor trader.
As of 11:30 EST, May heating oil was up 0.60 cent at 56.50 cents a barrel. Gasoline was down 0.30 at 62.20 and June crude was down seven cents at $19.92 a barrel.
Players said the expiry of the May contract on Wednesday forced speculators to roll their short positions forward, which means buying the May contract and selling June.
The spread between May and June was about 2.8 cents, up from 2.12 cents at the end of trading Friday.
"There was some aggressive buying on heating oil this morning with the expiry in three days. People wanted to flatten out their positions, rolling over into June," said a NYMEX heating oil trader.
Traders pegged resistance at about 56.70 cents but Pegasus Econometric Group said selling could reach the 57.25 cent peak set March 19.
Meanwhile, gasoline remained in the doldrums as a surfeit of supply and a lack of demand continued to weigh down prices.
"Everyone anticipated tremendous gasoline demand for the driving season but it's just not happening," said a trader. "There is plenty of supply around."

May gasoline, however, found some support on a bit of short-covering ahead of its contract expiry on Wednesday and short covering. May came off its low of 61.90 cents on Monday to a high of 62.50 cents.
NYMEX crude oil futures were only slightly down with traders saying the ongoing tribal unrest in one of Nigeria's oil-producing areas had little effect on the market.
The unrest caused some loss of production and delays in shipping some cargoes.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631
